newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament approves finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament approves finance minister.

text.p: Israel's parliament approved the appointment of lawyer Yaacov Neeman as finance minister on Wednesday. The vote was 52-46.

Neeman, a former Treasury director-general, was Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's surprise choice over ex-general Ariel Sharon, a champion of West Bank Jewish settlement whose candidacy rattled Arabs and Israel's ally the United States.

Parliament also approved Likud party Michael Eitan, a Netanyahu loyalist, as science minister. Analysts said Netanyahu's appointments now gave him a much more loyal cabinet but that by snubbing Sharon he had made a dangerous enemy within his own party.

"I think that parliament members can congratulate two talented and experienced people who will aid the work of the government," Netanyahu said in a brief address to parliament before the vote. Afterwards both ministers were sworn in.

Neeman's appointment was designed to defuse a three-week cabinet crisis sparked by the resignation of Netanyahu's Likud arch-rival Dan Meridor, who vacated the finance post in a power struggle over foreign exchange policy.

Sharon was tipped to win the Treasury and had also demanded he be included in an inner "kitchen cabinet" which hashes out Arab-Israeli peace strategy. His bid was thwarted by Foreign Minister David Levy, who forced Netanyahu to grant him formal control of peace talks and scrap the inner cabinet.
